title: Vector Field
body:
A [[Vector]] attached to every point of space, rather than one vector sitting on its own.
Formally a function $\mathbf{F} : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$, input a point, output an arrow.

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y) = \langle P(x,y),\, Q(x,y) \rangle
$$

This is the object all of [[Vector Calculus]] acts on. [[LINEAR ALGEBRA]] studies vectors that just
sit there; this course studies vectors that **vary from point to point**, and the two operators
[[Divergence]] and [[Curl]] exist to measure how.

## What they model

| Field | At each point |
|---|---|
| Velocity field | which way the fluid is moving, and how fast |
| Force field | the force a test particle would feel there |
| [[Gradient]] field | which way a scalar function increases fastest |
| Electric or magnetic field | the field itself, which is where the vocabulary comes from |

Fluid flow is the mental picture worth keeping, because every term in this block is named after it:
flow, [[Flux]], circulation, source, sink.

## Scalar field versus vector field

A **scalar field** assigns a number to each point (temperature in a room, $f(x,y,z)$). A **vector
field** assigns an arrow. The three operators of this course move between them:

| Operator | Takes | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| [[Gradient]] $\nabla f$ | scalar field | vector field |
| [[Divergence]] $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}$ | vector field | scalar field |
| [[Curl]] $\nabla \times \mathbf{F}$ | vector field | vector field |

Reading the table by output type tells you which one a formula must be, and catches most sign and
shape errors before you evaluate anything.

## Two identities worth knowing cold

$$
\nabla \times (\nabla f) = \mathbf{0} \qquad\qquad \nabla \cdot (\nabla \times \mathbf{F}) = 0
$$

"Curl of a gradient is zero" and "divergence of a curl is zero". Both come out of Clairaut's
theorem on mixed [[Partial Derivative|partials]] and both are load bearing: the first is why a
[[Conservative Vector Field]] is curl-free, and the second is why the flux of a curl through a
closed surface vanishes.

## Related

- [[Divergence]] and [[Curl]]: the two derivatives of a vector field
- [[Conservative Vector Field]]: the ones that are gradients of something
